headline: Chicago hoops is a Public League faith that claims players by high school and side of town (Simeon's Benji and Rose, Farragut's KG, Marshall's Hoop Dreams) and spends half the year in Park District fieldhouses because the Hawk shuts the outdoor courts.
summary: Chicago's basketball identity lives in the Chicago Public League (Simeon, Whitney Young, Farragut, Marshall, Morgan Park) and in suburban powers like Proviso East, and its canon is about loss and resilience, led by Simeon's Ben Wilson, the country's top high school player when he was killed in 1984. The game follows the weather: park and lakefront courts from May to September, Park District fieldhouses the rest of the year, and the season peaks in March when teams 'go downstate' for the IHSA finals, the tournament that gave basketball the phrase 'March Madness.' The market also has the WNBA's Chicago Sky, the G League's Windy City Bulls, DePaul and Loyola, and it hosts the NBA Draft Combine every May, so the hoops calendar never goes dark. Nike's opening is to build on what it already owns here (Mac Irvin Fire, the Bulls and Sky uniforms, the 'Chicago' color-blocking) in a city where many favorite sons, Derrick Rose first among them, wear rival brands.

insights.title: Claimed by school, then by side
insights.detail: Chicagoans introduce a player by high school before anything else: Simeon's Derrick Rose and Jabari Parker, Farragut's Kevin Garnett, Whitney Young's Quentin Richardson and Jahlil Okafor, Marshall's Cappie Pondexter and Patrick Beverley, Crane's Tony Allen, Proviso East's Doc Rivers and Michael Finley. Public League conferences are named by side of town (Red-South, Red-West), so a Simeon-Young city title game is also South Side against the Near West Side.
insights.implication: Make the school and the side the unit of storytelling: school-licensed shooting shirts and gym investments that name the program and the neighborhood, never a generic 'Chi-Town hooper.'

insights.title: Benji and No. 25 are sacred
insights.detail: Simeon's Ben Wilson was the nation's top-ranked high school player when he was shot near the school in November 1984, days before his senior season. His Simeon teammate Nick Anderson wore No. 25 at Illinois and in Orlando for him, and Derrick Rose wore it at Simeon. The city's hoops memory also holds near-misses like Farragut dunker Ronnie Fields.
insights.implication: Nike's role is to fund and amplify (Simeon's program, family-approved youth work), never to print 25 or the tragedy on product. Lead with resilience stories the people involved tell themselves.

insights.title: Fieldhouse city: the Hawk sends the game indoors
insights.detail: In 1905 the South Park Commission opened neighborhood parks with fieldhouses by D.H. Burnham & Co. and the Olmsted Brothers, a model copied across the country, and Park District fieldhouse gyms still carry winter leagues and open runs. Outdoor park and lakefront courts only really run from May to September, and spring and fall runs are played in hoodies under jerseys.
insights.implication: Plan two seasons of product: fieldhouse warmups for November to April and an outdoor drop in June. Refurbished fieldhouse floors do more good here than painted outdoor courts that spend months under snow.

insights.title: A Jordan city that grew up in Rose's adidas
insights.detail: Chicago is home to the 1985 Air Jordan 1 'Chicago' and still dresses its games in white, red and black, but a generation of South and West Side kids came up in adidas D Rose shoes and Rose's headband. Rose (adidas, plus the adidas-circuit Team Rose program), Candace Parker (adidas), Dwyane Wade (Li-Ning) and the Sky's Angel Reese (Reebok) mean many of the city's best-loved hoops names belong to rival brands.
insights.implication: Compete at the grassroots with assets Nike owns: Mac Irvin Fire in the EYBL, the Bulls and Sky uniforms, and 'Chicago' color-blocking. Never borrow Rose's No. 1 or his Englewood story without him and his sponsor.

insights.title: 'Going downstate' and keeping kids home
insights.detail: IHSA official H.V. Porter is credited with coining 'March Madness' for the Illinois high school tournament in 1939, and 'going downstate' (Peoria or Champaign over the years) is still the goal of every season. College loyalty turns on whether Chicago's best stay in-state: the 1989 'Flyin' Illini' Final Four team leaned on Simeon's Nick Anderson, King's Marcus Liberty and Rich Central's Kendall Gill, and Morgan Park's Ayo Dosunmu chose Illinois in 2018, while Rose, Parker and Okafor left the state for college.
insights.implication: Treat March as a second peak: a state-tournament capsule built on bracket graphics, with a 'stay home, rep home' message. The words 'March Madness' themselves are a licensed mark.

insights.title: The calendar keeps going after the Bulls stop
insights.detail: The Sky won Chicago's first WNBA title in 2021 with Naperville's Candace Parker and play at Wintrust Arena in the South Loop alongside DePaul, and Angel Reese and Kamilla Cardoso have made Sky games a hot ticket since 2024. The G League's Windy City Bulls play in Hoffman Estates, and the NBA Draft Combine comes to Chicago every May.
insights.implication: Nike makes both NBA and WNBA uniforms, so a Bulls-Sky 'one city' line can keep Chicago hoops product selling from May to September. Lead with the team and the uniform rather than with Reebok's Reese.

insights.title: Chicago tells its hoops stories as documentaries
insights.detail: Kartemquin Films' 'Hoop Dreams' (1994, directed by Steve James) followed William Gates and Arthur Agee from the West Side through St. Joseph and Marshall, and Chicago filmmakers Coodie Simmons and Chike Ozah made ESPN's 30 for 30 'Benji' (2012). The Sun-Times' high school coverage still sets the daily Public League conversation.
insights.implication: The native activation format is long-form film. Commission a paid, credited series with Kartemquin or Coodie & Chike that follows a current Public League team through a season, with product tied to its episodes.

places.name: Simeon Career Academy
places.why: The Public League's flagship program: Ben Wilson, Nick Anderson, Derrick Rose and Jabari Parker, with state titles across the Rose and Parker eras.

places.name: Murray Park
places.why: Derrick Rose's childhood park, where his older brothers brought him up in the game, and the court that ties Englewood to the 2011 MVP.

places.name: Whitney M. Young Magnet High School
places.why: The powerhouse closest to the United Center, about half a mile east on the West Side (Quentin Richardson, Jahlil Okafor), and Simeon's main Public League rival.

places.name: Farragut Career Academy
places.why: Where Kevin Garnett played his senior year (1994-95) alongside Ronnie Fields before going straight to the NBA, giving a mostly Mexican-American neighborhood a piece of hoops legend.

places.name: John Marshall Metropolitan High School
places.why: The school of 'Hoop Dreams' (Arthur Agee), Cappie Pondexter and Patrick Beverley, and of Dorothy Gaters' girls dynasty.

places.name: Proviso East High School
places.why: The suburban rival to the Public League: Doc Rivers, Michael Finley, Dee Brown and Shannon Brown all came through Maywood.

places.name: Wintrust Arena
places.why: Home of the Chicago Sky and DePaul and a recent site of the NBA Draft Combine, so it hosts more Chicago basketball than any building except the United Center.

places.name: NOW Arena
places.why: Home of the Windy City Bulls, the Bulls' G League affiliate, and the cheapest live pro basketball for northwest-suburban families.

people.name: Ben 'Benji' Wilson
people.role: Simeon star, the nation's top-ranked high school player in 1984 (died 1984)
people.why: Chicago's hoops patron saint: Nick Anderson and Derrick Rose wore his No. 25, and ESPN's 'Benji' made him a national story.

people.name: Derrick Rose
people.role: Englewood native, Simeon and Memphis, 2011 NBA MVP with the Bulls (retired 2024)
people.why: The South Side's own and the city's most loved homegrown Bull, but an adidas athlete, so any Rose story needs him and his sponsor.

people.name: Isiah Thomas
people.role: West Side native, St. Joseph (Westchester) and Indiana, Hall of Fame Pistons guard
people.why: A West Side son who led the 'Bad Boys' against Jordan's Bulls, so locals claim him with mixed feelings.

people.name: Jalen Brunson
people.role: Stevenson High School (Lincolnshire) 2015 state champion, 2026 NBA Finals MVP with the Knicks
people.why: The north suburbs claim the reigning Finals MVP, which leaves Bulls fans proud of the kid and wary of the jersey.

people.name: Candace Parker
people.role: Naperville Central, WNBA great, 2021 champion with the Chicago Sky
people.why: Came home to win Chicago's first WNBA title; now an adidas executive, so honor her through the Sky story and stay off her likeness.

people.name: Matas Buzelis
people.why: The 2026-27 core's homegrown face, in a city with one of the largest Lithuanian communities in the U.S.

people.name: Ronnie Fields
people.role: Farragut high-flyer and Kevin Garnett's teammate
people.why: Chicago's defining playground and 'what could have been' legend; his dunks are still retold years after a 1996 car crash derailed his NBA path.

people.name: Mac Irvin Fire
people.role: Nike EYBL grassroots program founded by Mac Irvin
people.why: Nike's own pipeline in Chicago and the program the city's top prospects have played for on the summer circuit.

moments.name: Proviso West Holiday Tournament
moments.timing: Between Christmas and New Year's, Hillside
moments.why: The Chicago area's long-running holiday showcase, where Public League, Catholic League and suburban powers first meet.

moments.name: Chicago Public League city championship
moments.why: The city title game, usually a South-vs-West or Simeon-vs-Young grudge match, decided before the state series.

moments.name: IHSA state finals ('going downstate')
moments.why: The original March Madness; whole neighborhoods follow their school downstate.

moments.name: Nike EYBL season
moments.timing: April to July, ending at Peach Jam
moments.why: Mac Irvin Fire carries Chicago's top prospects on Nike's own circuit.

moments.name: NBA Draft Combine
moments.why: The league's prospects, scouts and media spend a week in Chicago just after the Bulls' season ends.

moments.name: Chicago Sky season
moments.why: Gives the city a Nike-dressed home team through the summer.

moments.name: Summer park leagues and peace tournaments
moments.why: Park District leagues and church-led peace tournaments, such as St. Sabina's, use basketball for violence interruption on the South and West Sides.

moments.name: Windy City Bulls season
moments.why: The G League affiliate where Bulls prospects develop, close to home for suburban families.

vocabulary.meaning: The Chicago Public Schools league; its top conferences are named by side of town.
Making the IHSA state finals, held in Peoria or Champaign over the years: 'Simeon's going downstate again.'
Ben Wilson; '25 for Benji' is the city's most sacred hoops tribute.
Chicago slang for excellent: 'that crossover was pressure.'
Any younger player, boy or girl: 'let shorty run next.'
The cutting wind off Lake Michigan; when the Hawk is out, the run moves to the fieldhouse.
A Park District building with a gym, the default winter run: 'meet at the fieldhouse.'
Sneakerhead shorthand for the white, red and black Air Jordan 1 'Chicago' colorway.

designCues.cue: Fieldhouse brick: the dark red-brown face brick of the 1905 South Park fieldhouses and later Park District gyms.
designCues.source: Chicago Park District fieldhouses designed by D.H. Burnham & Co. and the Olmsted Brothers
designCues.use: Base color for a winter warmup line, piped in Bulls red #CE1141 and black.

designCues.cue: Varnished maple: the deep amber of old fieldhouse floors under yellow gym lights.
designCues.source: Park District and Public League gym floors
designCues.use: Collar tape, hood linings and tonal floor-board graphics on shooting shirts.

designCues.cue: 'Chicago' color-blocking: white body, Bulls red #CE1141 overlays and black accents, in the panel logic of the 1985 Air Jordan 1.
designCues.source: The city's de facto hoops uniform, owned by Nike
designCues.use: Reversible practice jerseys and shooting shirts, with Jordan Brand for any Jumpman or Michael Jordan reference.

designCues.cue: Side-of-town tags: 'RED-SOUTH' and 'RED-WEST' stacked in condensed athletic block over a school's street number, like a gym banner.
designCues.source: Public League conference names and the city's numbered grid
designCues.use: School-partnership tees and warmups, made with each program and under CPS licensing.

designCues.cue: Downstate bracket: thin single-elimination bracket lines converging on Champaign, marked 'EST. 1939.'
designCues.source: The Illinois high school tournament that coined 'March Madness'
designCues.use: March capsule graphic, made with the IHSA; avoid the 'March Madness' wordmark.

designCues.cue: Hawk layer: a hooded shooting shirt cut to wear like a hoodie under a jersey, with a wind-blocking front panel and thumbhole cuffs.
designCues.source: April and October outdoor runs in lake wind
designCues.use: Outdoor court wear for the shoulder seasons, with a Bulls red-lined hood.

designCues.cue: Savoy Big Five: the Harlem Globetrotters began in 1926-27 as Chicago's Savoy Big Five, playing at Bronzeville's Savoy Ballroom on South Parkway (now King Drive).
designCues.use: A heritage capsule with wool-look warmups, felt chenille lettering and ballroom-era script, made with Bronzeville historians and institutions; no Globetrotters marks without a license.

productHooks: Fieldhouse Collection: winter warmups in fieldhouse brick and varnished maple, launched in January alongside refurbished floors in Park District fieldhouse gyms on the South and West Sides, co-branded with the Chicago Park District.
Public League Pride: licensed shooting shirts for Simeon, Whitney Young, Farragut, Marshall and Morgan Park, with proceeds to each program, dropped the week of the February city championship.
Downstate '39: a March bracket capsule made with the IHSA, plus custom tees for every Chicago-area team that goes downstate.
Hawk Layer: a hooded shooting shirt for April and October outdoor runs, red-lined to pair with the Bulls Statement uniform.
Combine Week Run: during the May NBA Draft Combine, a Nike-hosted run at a West Side fieldhouse with Mac Irvin Fire players, followed by a Chicago-only drop.
One City summer pack: Bulls and Sky reversible practice jerseys and shorts, sold from the Sky's May tip-off through Labor Day.
watchouts: Rival-brand legends: Derrick Rose and Team Rose (adidas), Candace Parker (adidas), Dwyane Wade (Li-Ning) and Angel Reese (Reebok). Don't use their names, numbers, likeness or personal stories on Nike product.

Gun violence runs through Chicago's hoops canon (Ben Wilson). Never market with it, and never use 'Chiraq,' drill or gang slang, or ski-mask imagery. Peace-league work should be led and credited by its organizers and funded for years, not one summer.

Licensed IP: 'March Madness' (a registered mark tied to the NCAA and IHSA), IHSA, CPS and school marks, 'Hoop Dreams' (Kartemquin), 'Benji' (ESPN), Harlem Globetrotters marks and Chicago Park District marks.
Rival-team sons: Isiah Thomas (the Bad Boys) and Jalen Brunson (the Knicks) belong to their high schools and neighborhoods, not to Bulls-branded product.
Don't flatten Lincolnshire or Naperville into the South and West Sides. Public League gyms face real resource gaps, so put floors, uniforms and money there first.
